subject: Acme MAP recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Stevens <john.stevens@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Acme MAP recap & next steps

Hi John / Priya \u001f

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we discussed below. I tried to capture the key pain, goals, stakeholders, and tentative timeline so we can align next steps. Please flag anything I missed or misinterpreted.

Pain points we heard:
- Current inference costs have spiked ~3x after increased query volumes; ops spend is focused on workarounds (manual model routing, ad-hoc batching)
- Latency tail during peak windows impacting user experience (p95 ~1.2s on critical flows)
- Lack of visibility into per-route token spend and difficulty correlating regressions to model changes

Goals / success criteria:
- Reduce per-token cost by 30% through batching, caching, and quantization suggestions
- Achieve p95 latency <= 600ms for the customer-facing search flow under expected peak load
- Visibility: token-level cost breakdown + alerts on quality regressions tied to eval prompt sets

Stakeholders / decision process:
- John Stevens \u001f VP Product (final decision sponsor)
- Priya Shah \u001f Head of ML Platforms (technical evals + PoC lead)
- Procurement (TBD) \u001f contract negotiation & SOW
- Redwood contacts: Marissa (you), Stephanie (legal/pricing support), Dev (solutions engineer)

Proposed MAP + milestones (draft):
1) Week 0 (this week): Align on scope & PoC success criteria \u001f finalize PoC dataset and acceptance tests (owner: Priya) \u001f target 2026-03-01
2) Week 1-2: PoC run on Redwood Dedicated (sandbox) \u001f measure latency/cost delta; implement prefix/KV caching for hot routes (owner: Dev) \u001f target 2026-03-15
3) Week 3: Quality validation + regression checks against eval prompt set; show token-cost dashboards (owner: Marissa/Dev) \u001f target 2026-03-22
4) Week 4-5: SOW & procurement review, finalize pricing/commit (owner: Procurement / Stephanie) \u001f target 2026-04-05
5) Week 6: Production rollout plan & handoff to Acme infra (owner: Priya / Redwood) \u001f target 2026-04-19

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Priya: confirm PoC dataset and any IP/PHI constraints by 2026-02-27
- John: share procurement timeline / preferred SOW terms (if already known)
- Redwood (Dev): schedule PoC kickoff and share runbook + required access checklist

I've attached a draft MAP spreadsheet and a placeholder SOW to help with internal alignment.

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP draft), SOW_Draft_Acme.pdf (placeholder)

Thanks again \u001f look forward to moving quickly on this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0143

--
Redwood Inference \u001f developer-first inference for production LLMs
From: John Stevens <john.stevens@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme MAP recap & next steps

Marissa \u001f thanks for the thorough recap. That maps to our discussion. A couple of quick clarifications / adjustments:

1) PoC dataset: we'll provide a 7-day sample of traffic (anonymized) but note that some requests include customer identifiers we cannot share. Priya will confirm which fields must be removed.
2) Timeline: procurement at Acme is tight \u001f we need a draft SOW by 2026-03-05 to present to the procurement committee on 2026-03-10.
3) Success criteria: please include an explicit cost-per-1000-requests number change in the MAP so we can compare against our baseline.

We're comfortable with Redwood running the PoC in a sandbox/dedicated environment. Priya and I will schedule a technical kickoff next week.

Also: for the SOW, can you include standard security controls (SOC 2, data retention, key management) and a template for logging/audit evidence so procurement can do a preliminary review?

Thanks \u001f John

On Thu, Feb 26, 2026 at 08:15 AM Priya Shah <priya@acme.com> wrote:

Thanks John \u001f appreciate the clarifications. Quick update and tightened MAP below; I also attached the updated MAP spreadsheet that includes the PoC success criteria with explicit cost-per-1k baseline numbers and the SOW placeholder with SOC 2 / logging language called out.

What I changed:
- PoC acceptance criteria row now shows baseline cost: $28.40 / 1k requests -> target <= $19.88 / 1k requests (30% reduction)
- Added procurement milestone: Draft SOW delivered 2026-03-04 (so you have time before your 03-10 committee)
- Security appendix in SOW includes: SOC 2 Type II, KMS integration options, audit log export cadence (30 days by default; options to extend)

Updated MAP milestones & owners (short):
- 2026-03-01: Priya confirms anonymization fields (owner: Priya)
- 2026-03-08: PoC kickoff & Redwood runbook shared (owner: Dev)
- 2026-03-15: Mid-PoC check \u001f latency & cost preliminary results (owner: Dev / Marissa)
- 2026-03-22: Final PoC results + quality regression report (owner: Marissa / Dev)
- 2026-03-04: Draft SOW delivered to Acme procurement (owner: Stephanie)
- 2026-04-05: Final SOW & contract sign (target)

Next immediate asks:
- Priya: confirm anonymization fields by 2026-03-01 (reply to thread)
- John: confirm procurement committee date (is 2026-03-10 final?)
- Stephanie: I copied you on the SOW delivery; can you confirm we can deliver the draft by 2026-03-04?

Attachments (updated): Acme_MAP_v2.xlsx, SOW_Draft_Acme.pdf

If all good, I'll lock the MAP and coordinate the PoC kickoff with Dev.
